title: On-call transfer & postmortem flow — Console UX for alerts to incident lifecycle
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: On-call engineers and incident responders need faster context and lower friction when transferring ownership mid-incident and when filing postmortems. Current Console flows separate alert rules, on-call rotations, and postmortem docs which slows triage and creates noise in SLO investigations.

Goal: Design a cohesive incident lifecycle surface in Console that: 1) surfaces runbooks and alert context at alert-setup time, 2) provides a lightweight ‘On-call Handoff Card’ in the incident timeline with actionable buttons (claim, escalate, message current on-call), and 3) scaffolds a postmortem draft pre-populated with alert metadata, SLO snapshots, and links to relevant dashboards. The flow should be usable by engineers, SREs, and PMs with minimal clicks and clear audit trails for compliance.

Scope: UI/UX for alert setup modal, incident timeline card, handoff microcopy, postmortem scaffold modal, and small Console settings changes to store runbook templates and on-call integration preferences. Prototype includes desktop and narrow-screen responsive states; we will not ship mobile-first in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Alert setup modal includes a required 'runbook' field (URL or snippet) and an optional on-call rotation selector
Incident timeline displays an 'On-call Handoff Card' with user, timestamp, and three CTAs: Claim, Message, Create Postmortem
Create Postmortem pre-populates title, alert rule, first 10 lines of logs (link to dashboard), SLO snapshot, and a link to the PR/commit if provided
Prototype validated with at least 4 engineering/SRE participants with no major usability blockers
Design assets (Figma) and implementation notes delivered to ENG-2238 and PM-398 and include edge-case handling for cross-region rotation mappings
updates: 2025-02-14 — Aisha Patel: Initial draft of flows and acceptance criteria. Spike with SREs scheduled for 2025-02-17.

2025-02-17 — Usability session notes: interviewed 4 responders (Hannah Price, Luis Martinez, Sofia Gomez, Rajiv Sen). Key findings: (1) Runbook must be visible before claim, (2) 'Claim' should include ETA and optional note, (3) Postmortem scaffold should allow toggling to 'private' mode for internal incidents.

2025-02-18 — Design update: added 'ETA' field to claim flow, added runbook preview in alert setup, created alternative compact handoff card for high-alert-volume orgs. Shared new frames in Figma and requested eng input on API for prepopulating logs.

2025-02-19 — Engineering feedback (Luis Martinez): prefer smaller payloads in initial release; suggested linking to log snapshot instead of embedding top logs due to token and storage constraints. Adjusted acceptance criteria accordingly.

2025-02-20 — PM review (Sofia Gomez): Approved prototype conceptually; asked for copy edits around escalation language and a way to surface 'last acknowledged by' in the handoff card. Marked ticket In Review and requested one more quick usability check with on-call rotation owners.
design_decisions: Include runbook as a required field at alert creation to reduce lost context during first responder triage — trade-off: higher friction for rule creators but reduces mean-time-to-recovery.

Use 'link-to-dashboard' for log/context snapshots in initial release instead of embedded logs to avoid storage/token costs — trade-off: extra click for responders but simpler backend and faster iterations.
On-call Handoff Card will be immutable in timeline after an owner claim to preserve audit trail; allow follow-up 'transfer' actions that append to the timeline rather than mutating the original card.
Postmortem scaffold will be optional and stored in Console as a draft with export to Confluence/GDrive — avoids forcing teams into a single toolchain but provides a consistent starting point.
Default postmortem visibility is 'team-only' with an explicit toggle to 'public' to meet compliance/PR needs.
Compact vs. full handoff card: default to full for first rollout, allow org-level preference for compact in admin settings.
Copy will use urgency-neutral language (e.g., 'Claim incident' not 'Take over now') after SRE feedback to avoid escalation-induced anxiety during on-call rotations.
feedback_from_reviews: Hannah Price (SRE): Add 'Acknowledge' vs 'Claim' distinction in copy and visual affordance to prevent accidental ownership transfers.
Luis Martinez (Eng): Implementation note — need API endpoint to return 'rotation person at time T' for historical accuracy in timelines.
Sofia Gomez (PM): Ensure postmortem template has sections for 'User Impact', 'SLO delta', 'Mitigation timeline', and 'Action items with owners'
Design leadership (Jared Chen): Suggest moving 'runbook' UI out of the tiny alert rule modal into an expandable side panel for better editing UX.
next_steps: Finalize copy edits and update Figma frames (Marco Li) — due 2025-02-21
Align with ENG-2238 on API contract for postmortem scaffold and rotation lookup (Luis Martinez) — sync 2025-02-22
Run one more 20-minute usability validation with 3 on-call responders (Aisha to schedule) — target 2025-02-24
Add admin toggle for compact handoff card to Console settings RFC (PM-398) — PM to draft by 2025-02-26
Prepare handoff package for implementation: Figma tokens, redlines, and acceptance criteria, then move to Planned for ENG work.
